name: Lennart Meri Tallinn Airport
before:
Estonia's main airport, and one of the easiest capital arrivals in Europe. It is 5 km south east of the centre of Tallinn, on the eastern shore of Lake Ulemiste, so the transfer is short whichever way a client travels.

Everything runs from a single passenger terminal with seventeen gates, alongside four cargo terminals. The runway is 3,480 metres, long enough for a 747, which is more capability than the traffic needs and means weather diversions and the occasional large charter are straightforward.

One oddity worth knowing about. The Estonian EXPO Center keeps a permanent exhibition near Gate 3, opened in 2010, where companies show what they do to passengers waiting to board. It is a trade display rather than a shop, and there is nothing quite like it in another European terminal.

The airport is officially named after Lennart Meri, a former president of Estonia, and was called Tallinn Ulemiste until 2009, so older references use that name.
after:
Estonia's main airport, and one of the easiest capital arrivals in Europe. It is 5 km south east of the centre of Tallinn, on the shore of Lake Ülemiste, so the transfer is short whichever way a client travels.

Passenger flights all use a single terminal. The runway is 3,480 metres, which is more than the everyday traffic needs.

It has carried the name of Lennart Meri, a former president of Estonia, since 2009, though the operator still uses plain Tallinn Airport as well.

claims.note: Eurostat reports no other Estonian airport for 2025 (the file header lists every EE airport it reports, high to low: Tallinn alone). The operator runs the regional airports too.

claims.claim: long enough for a 747; weather diversions and large charters straightforward
claims.wasBefore: long enough for a 747, which is more capability than the traffic needs and means weather diversions and the occasional large charter are straightforward.
claims.why: The 747 rests on Wikipedia alone; the operator's pages read (its about page and its aviation charges page) do not describe the runway. The diversions and charters lean on it, so they go too. The runway length and the old text's judgement on it are kept.

claims.claim: the Estonian EXPO Center near Gate 3, opened 2010; nothing like it in Europe
claims.wasBefore: One oddity worth knowing about. The Estonian EXPO Center keeps a permanent exhibition near Gate 3, opened in 2010, where companies show what they do to passengers waiting to board. It is a trade display rather than a shop, and there is nothing quite like it in another European terminal.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and the airport's own terminal map (read 23 Sep 2026) shows no exhibition, so it may no longer be there. The 'nothing quite like it' judgement rests on it.

claims.wasBefore: and was called Tallinn Ulemiste until 2009, so older references use that name.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's own sentence has Tallinn Airport, not Ülemiste, renamed in 2009. Replaced with the operator's own use of the plain name (see above).

Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing. Eurostat has 3,472,035 passengers in 2025 (3,471,878 in 2024), and Wikipedia says the terminal served over 3.5 million in 2025. Wikipedia alone also has trams T2 and T4 back at the terminal from 1 August 2026; that would need a second source before use.
